_comment: Recorded per ROADMAP.md chunk 3's 'Done when'. Rows-written measured with SqlStorageCursor.rowsWritten inside a real DO instance (runInDurableObject); CPU measured as wall-clock schnorr.verify() time, which is the dominant cost of Worker CPU per NIP-01 EVENT (see CLAUDE.md 'The budget': 'Schnorr verification is the CPU risk'). Re-measure and update this file whenever a change could plausibly shift either number -- see CLAUDE.md 'Testing'.

rows_written_per_event.note: Was 3 + 2*tags until v0.7.2, which added idx_events_kind_created and idx_events_pubkey_created to `events` to fix the rows-READ exhaustion (see rows_read_per_call below). Each index costs one row per insert, so the base went 3 -> 5. `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` is not a rowid alias and still costs its own implicit unique index on top. NOT inferred from counting index declarations: schema.ts eventRowCost derives the figure from INDEXES, and test/hibernation.test.ts asserts that derivation against real SqlStorageCursor.rowsWritten on the real storeEvent path, for a bare note, a two-tag reply, and an event carrying a multi-character tag that is stored but never indexed.
rows_written_per_event.cost_of_the_read_fix: +2 rows per stored event. At the live relay's ~2,900 events/day that is ~5,800 rows/day against a 100,000/day ceiling metered at ~38,000, taking it to ~44,000.

schnorr_verify_cpu.note: Measured with @noble/curves' schnorr.verify() directly (scripts run outside the miniflare/workerd harness, which doesn't expose isolate CPU time to test code). workerd's JS engine is also V8, so this is a reasonable proxy, but re-measure against real wrangler dev / production logs before treating the 10ms ceiling as comfortably clear rather than just plausible.

rows_read_per_call._comment: Measured with SqlStorageCursor.rowsRead inside a real DO (test/read-cost.test.ts), the same mechanism the rows_written figures above used. E = rows in `events`, T = rows in `event_tags` (~5E for real notes). Sample column is at E=2000, T=10000. `before` is the v0.7.1 cost that exhausted the 5,000,000 rows-read/day allowance; `after` is v0.7.2. Where an index is what changed, `before` is measured live by suppressing index use with SQLite's unary + operator against the same rows, not quoted from the older run.

req_filter_authors_and_one_kind.note: The control. Served by idx_events_pubkey_kind_created and never the problem; if this regresses the index set has been broken rather than extended.

gift_wrap_gate_probe.note: Unchanged from the chunk 6 measurement in CLAUDE.md's budget section.

estimate_rows_written_24h.formula_before: E + T (E only when nothing was ingested in the window)
estimate_rows_written_24h.note: The LEFT JOIN on event_tags.event_id had no index -- idx_event_tags_lookup is (tag_name, tag_value, created_at) -- so SQLite built an automatic index over the whole of event_tags on every call, reading every tag row to answer a question about the 10 rows in the window. Now sums the per-event row_cost column stamped at insert time. Still E rather than the size of the window: `ingested_at` is covered by no index and must not be, since an index there would cost a row write per event, the exact cost the column exists to avoid.

get_stats_total.formula_after: ~4E on a cache miss, ~0 within STATS_CACHE_TTL_MS
get_stats_total.note: relay.ts statsCache memoizes the counts for 15s. The remaining 4E on a miss is three COUNT scans plus the estimate; `created_at` leads no index, so events24h cannot be narrowed without a fourth index. The 1 row on a cached load is recordHost, deliberately left outside the cache.

backfill_tick.formula: 2 x estimateRowsWritten24h + ~2 per event in the page
backfill_tick.note: hasBackfillHeadroom calls the estimate twice per tick -- once in getBackfillState so the Worker can skip opening a socket, once inside applyBackfillPage authoritatively. Both still get a fresh answer; the stats cache is deliberately not on this path, since it decides whether writes may proceed.

live_write_replaceable_replacement.note: NOT FIXED, and recorded so it stays visible. `DELETE FROM event_tags WHERE event_id = ?` (storage.ts deleteEventRow) is a full scan; no index covers event_id. Paid on every kind-0/kind-3/kind-10002/NIP-51/addressable republish and every NIP-09/NIP-62/banevent deletion. This path spends 5E x R rows/day and reaches the 5,000,000 ceiling at E x R = 1,000,000, so it is the binding constraint for any R above ~10/day -- sooner than the cron floor, which now binds at E ~= 104,000. The reasoning, the arithmetic and the estimate of R are in the comment on deleteEventRow in src/storage.ts, beside the query. read-metrics.ts counts replacements so R can be read off /api/stats rather than estimated.

gift_wrap_count.note: storage.ts giftWrapCount, run on every accepted gift wrap. `kind` led no index; fixed as a side effect of idx_events_kind_created.

init_schema_per_do_constructor.note: Paid per wake from hibernation, not once per deploy.

req_filter_kinds_only.note: idx_events_kind_created serves ORDER BY created_at DESC directly, so LIMIT stops the scan. The property that was missing before is that asking for less now costs less.

req_filter_authors_only.note: idx_events_pubkey_created. On a single-owner relay every row carries the owner's pubkey, so this shape was a request for the whole table with a limit that bounded nothing.

req_filter_multi_kind.note: An index can only serve the sort when every key column ahead of created_at is pinned to ONE value, and `kind IN (1,7)` pins nothing -- so a multi-kind filter defeated the new index as thoroughly as no index at all. filters.ts expandFilter runs one limited query per (author, kind) combination and storage.ts queryFilter re-merges and re-slices, which is also what makes the cost independent of which index the planner picks.

cron_floor_per_day.note: What the relay spends per day with no client connected at all. At 288E the entire 5,000,000 ceiling was consumed by the cron alone at E ~= 17,400; at 48E that point moves to E ~= 104,000.

replacements_counter.what: R -- replaceable/addressable replacements per day, counted in memory by read-metrics.ts countReplacement and reported as `reads.replacements` on /api/stats.
replacements_counter.why: The per-call cost of the event_tags delete is measured and known; how often it is paid is not, and estimating it lands on a range spanning the point where the path overtakes the cron floor. `ceilingAtEvents` in that report is 1,000,000 / R -- the table size at which this path alone reaches 5,000,000 rows read per day.
replacements_counter.excludes: NIP-09 deletions, NIP-62 vanish requests and NIP-86 banevent. They reach the same DELETE and pay the same cost, but at operator pace rather than on the per-event drumbeat R measures; counting them would inflate the number the fix decision turns on.
